subject.title: [codex] Verify Telegram topic proof for cron delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept a plugin-facing `validateDeliveryResults` hook plus fail-closed Telegram non-General topic semantics for cron delivery proof after the fallback bug is fixed?
rationale: This changes the plugin SDK surface and can turn an already-sent Telegram payload into a failed delivery, so code correctness alone does not settle the API and upgrade-policy choice.

options.title: Accept Shared Hook After Repair
options.body: Fix the rich fallback proof bug, keep the documented SDK hook, and explicitly own fail-closed post-send validation semantics for Telegram topics.

options.title: Keep Validation Telegram-Internal
options.body: Ask the contributor to remove the shared hook and implement provider-proof validation behind Telegram-owned delivery code only.

options.title: Pause For Topic-Routing Consolidation
options.body: Wait for the overlapping Telegram topic-routing PR to settle, then decide whether this provider-proof hook still belongs as a separate branch.

recommendation.title: Accept Shared Hook After Repair
recommendation.body: Fix the rich fallback proof bug, keep the documented SDK hook, and explicitly own fail-closed post-send validation semantics for Telegram topics.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the earlier channel-plugin topic parser boundary work and merged the adjacent cron thread-id persistence fix, making him the best available routing owner for the SDK/cron boundary decision.
